newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya sells t-bills despite shilling fall.
newsitem.headline: Kenya sells t-bills despite shilling fall.

text.p: Kenya's central bank sold $71 million in treasury bills at Thursday's auction, despite the Kenyan shilling's fall to an official record low against the dollar.
The bank sold 5.012 billion shillings ($71 million) of treasury bills compared to 7.341 billion shillings last week.

"We were expecting the worst to happen -- like rates to shoot up to 20 percent, but we got enough to finance the roll over of bills next week," William Nyagaka, manager of the national debt division told Reuters.
The average yield on benchmark 91-day t-bill eased to 18.199 percent from 18.220 percent.
The lower yield offered on the bills dashed speculation the government would use this week's auction to raise interest rates to keep investors from pulling out of treasury bills.
Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi said on Thursday the government was revising its budget and would possibly accept higher rates for treasury bills to help meet its expenditure.

The shilling, extending the slide that began when the International Monetary Fund (IMF) halted a key aid package last week citing corruption, fell 4.08 percent on Thursday to close at a commercial average of 70.26 to the dollar.
Analysts said a higher yield on government treasury bonds was bound to attract foreign investors and bring in much needed dollars to bolster the fragile shilling.
"It definitely didn't happen in this auction, but it is an indicator that treasury bills will be now the place to put your money in," said an analyst of Mudavadi's statement.
The bank sold 4.968 billion shillings of 91-day t-bills and 44 million shillings of the 182-day t-bills at 19.062 percent.
Last week, the bank sold 6.210 billion shillings of the 91-day bills and 1.130 billion shillings of the 182-day bills at 19.244 percent. ($1=70.26 Kenyan shillings)
